about.title: Gridley Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Gridley is a small Butte County community, but its stretch of Rt 99 along with local streets like Magnolia, Spruce, and Sycamore still see a steady stream of injury collisions — 11 in the most recent recorded year alone. Crashes here tend to cluster on Wednesday evenings, often tied to commuter and after-work traffic patterns. Whether you were rear-ended near a Rt 99 interchange or sideswiped on Sycamore Street, the aftermath can be disorienting: medical appointments, missed work, and an insurance adjuster calling before you've even seen a doctor. LawProactive isn't a law firm, but we connect Gridley residents with independent personal injury attorneys who handle these claims on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Our goal is simple — get you talking to someone who can protect your interests early, while evidence is still fresh and your rights are still fully intact.

whyChoose.title: Why Gridley Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Time Limits Matter
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim, but that window shrinks dramatically — sometimes to six months — if a government entity, like a public road authority, was involved. Connecting with an attorney early helps make sure that deadline never sneaks up on you.

items.title: Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly responsible for the crash, though your share of fault reduces the payout. An independent attorney can help make sure fault isn't unfairly pinned on you before you've had a chance to tell your side.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Backfire
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash, but anything you say can later be used to minimize your claim. Speaking with an attorney first, rather than the other driver's insurer, helps protect what you're entitled to under California law, which places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash on Rt 99 near Gridley — what should I do first?
items.answer: Seek medical care first, even if injuries seem minor, since some symptoms take days to appear. Try to document the scene with photos and get contact information for any witnesses. After that, avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer and consider talking to an independent attorney before settling anything.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Gridley?
items.answer: In California, you generally have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. That deadline can shrink to as little as six months if your claim involves a government entity, such as a city road or public agency, so it's worth having someone review your situation promptly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame for the crash. Your final recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, so it's still worth exploring your options with an attorney rather than assuming you have no case.
